title: Mixed-workload latency performance standard (short + long prompt co-scheduling)
author: Jonas Weber
body:
## Purpose
This standard defines **required mixed-workload benchmark scenarios** and **pass/fail performance gates** for changes that can affect tail latency when **short/interactive requests** are co-scheduled with **long-context (prefill-heavy) requests**.

The immediate driver is the Serving Runtime mixed-workload scheduler prototype, but the standard applies broadly to any runtime change that could alter queueing, batching, kernel selection, admission control, or prefill/decode overlap behavior.

## Why we need a dedicated mixed-workload standard
Single-class benchmarks (all-short or all-long) often miss the production failure mode we see in traces and customer reports:
- Short requests experience elevated **p95/p99 end-to-end latency** when long-context requests accumulate and dominate prefill.
- Under bursty traffic, a FIFO or batch-first policy can cause **priority inversion** (short requests stuck behind long prefill service).
- The system may look “fine” on average throughput while the interactive tail degrades.

This standard makes mixed workload performance a first-class gating requirement.

## Scope (when this standard must be run)
Required for PRs/releases that change any of the following in the serving runtime or its immediate dependencies:
1) Scheduler, queueing, dispatch policy, or fairness/backpressure behavior
2) Continuous batching policies that influence prefill grouping or decode interleaving
3) KV-cache management changes that influence prefill cost distribution or reclaim behavior
4) Kernel selection heuristics that can materially change prefill throughput or latency
5) Admission control policies, per-route limits, or class-based throttling

Suggested (not required) for:
- Model onboarding changes (new default quantization / kernels) that may alter prefill-heavy behavior
- GPU driver/runtime upgrades when prefill performance variance is suspected

## Definitions
**Short/interactive** (S-class): Requests whose primary success criterion is tail latency (TTFT and end-to-end). Typical: chat, agent steps, tool calls.

**Long/prefill-heavy** (L-class): Requests that are dominated by prefill compute. Typical: summarization with long context, retrieval-augmented prompts with large context windows.

**TTFT**: Time to first token (for streaming endpoints). If an endpoint is non-streaming, TTFT is approximated as first-byte time.

**E2E latency**: From request admission to last token/response completion.

**Throughput**:
- tokens/s at the runtime (preferred)
- requests/s (acceptable only if output token distributions are stable)

**Mixed-workload tail regression**: A statistically significant increase in S-class p95/p99 latency that occurs in mixed scenarios but may not appear in single-class benchmarks.

## Required benchmark scenarios
All scenarios below must be executed for scheduler/queueing/backpressure changes. For other changes in scope, scenarios may be reduced by perf owner discretion, but must include at least one steady mixed and one burst mixed scenario.

### Common configuration (applies to all scenarios)
- **Model set** (minimum):
  - 1× “general” chat model used in production baseline (e.g., 7B–13B class)
  - 1× long-context capable model config (same architecture if possible) to exercise prefill scaling
- **Hardware SKU** (minimum):
  - Primary: NVIDIA L40S or A100-80GB (whichever is current perf baseline)
  - Secondary (optional but recommended for release candidates): H100
- **Batching**: Use standard continuous batching defaults for the runtime version unless the change under test modifies batching.
- **Warmup**: 5 minutes minimum, excluded from measurements.
- **Measurement window**: 20 minutes minimum steady-state, plus scenario-specific burst segments.
- **Repetitions**: ≥ 3 runs per scenario; report median and run-to-run variance.
- **Sample size**: For S-class, ≥ 20,000 requests per run (or perf owner-approved equivalent) to make p99 meaningful.

### Scenario MW-1: Steady mixed (80/20) – interactive-dominant
**Intent:** Detect interactive tail regression in the common “mostly chat with background long jobs” pattern.
- Mix: 80% S-class / 20% L-class
- Arrival: Poisson (steady rate)
- Concurrency: Set so baseline GPU utilization sits ~65–75% (prevents false positives from saturated-only behavior)
- L-class prompt distribution: p50 6k tokens, p95 16k tokens (or closest feasible based on model limit)
- S-class prompt distribution: p50 200 tokens, p95 800 tokens
- Output tokens: keep stable (e.g., S-class p50 120, L-class p50 250)

### Scenario MW-2: Balanced mixed (50/50) – contention-heavy steady state
**Intent:** Stress fairness and queue discipline under sustained contention.
- Mix: 50% S-class / 50% L-class
- Arrival: steady
- Concurrency: Baseline GPU utilization ~75–85%
- L-class prompt distribution: p50 8k, p95 20k
- S-class prompt distribution: p50 300, p95 1k

### Scenario MW-3: Burst mixed – long burst over interactive base load
**Intent:** Reproduce the “long batch window” failure mode: interactive tail spikes during long-context bursts.
- Base load: S-class steady at rate R
- Burst: L-class surge for 90 seconds every 5 minutes (repeat at least 3 times)
- Concurrency: Choose R such that base steady utilization is ~55–65%; during bursts system should approach ~90% utilization but must not enter uncontrolled backlog growth.

### Scenario MW-4: Overload mixed – controlled degradation and starvation detection
**Intent:** Validate backpressure/admission control and ensure we do not starve L-class indefinitely.
- Mix: 70% S-class / 30% L-class
- Arrival: step increase into overload (target ~110–120% of sustainable tokens/s)
- Duration: 10 minutes overload segment, then return to steady for recovery observation
- Required outputs:
  - backlog growth rate
  - recovery time once overload ends
  - starvation signals (max wait, age distribution)

## Required metrics to record (per scenario)
Metrics must be broken out by class (S vs L) and also reported globally.

### Latency
- S-class:
  - TTFT p50/p95/p99
  - E2E p50/p95/p99
  - Queue wait p50/p95/p99 (enqueue → dispatch)
  - Service time p50/p95/p99 (dispatch → completion)
- L-class:
  - E2E p50/p95/p99
  - Queue wait p50/p95/p99
  - Service time p50/p95/p99

### Throughput / efficiency
- Total tokens/s (preferred) and/or GPU-seconds per 1M tokens (if available)
- Decode tokens/s (if split exists)
- Prefill tokens/s (if split exists)
- GPU utilization (avg + p95)

### Stability / queue health
- Queue depth p50/p95/max per class
- Max queue age per class
- Drop/timeout rates (client visible) per class
- Retries (if applicable)

## Pass/fail gates (CI and release readiness)
Gates are evaluated as deltas versus the current pinned baseline for the same model/SKU/scenario set.

### Gate A: Mixed-workload interactive tail latency (S-class)
Applies to MW-1, MW-2, MW-3.

Fail if any of the following are true (for any scenario):
1) **S-class E2E p95 regression** > **+8%** OR **+25 ms**, whichever is larger
2) **S-class TTFT p95 regression** > **+10%** OR **+20 ms**, whichever is larger
3) **S-class E2E p99 regression** > **+10%** OR **+40 ms**, whichever is larger

Notes:
- Both relative (%) and absolute (ms) thresholds are used to prevent false failures at very low latencies while still protecting customers at higher baselines.
- For non-streaming endpoints, substitute first-byte time for TTFT.

### Gate B: No starvation of long prompts (L-class fairness)
Applies to MW-2, MW-3, MW-4.

Fail if any of the following are true:
1) L-class **max queue wait** exceeds **30 s** for more than **0.1%** of L-class requests
2) L-class **E2E p99 regression** > **+15%** (unless explicitly approved as an experiment)
3) Under MW-4 overload segment, L-class completion rate drops below **60%** of baseline completion rate (signals pathological prioritization)

Rationale:
- We prioritize interactive latency, but must preserve bounded unfairness and avoid indefinite L-class starvation.

### Gate C: Throughput regression bounds
Applies to all mixed scenarios.

Fail if any of the following are true:
1) **Total tokens/s** regression > **-5%** in MW-1 or MW-2
2) **Total tokens/s** regression > **-8%** in MW-3 (burst scenarios can pay slightly more overhead)
3) Under MW-4 (overload), system does not recover to within **-3%** of baseline tokens/s within **5 minutes** after returning to steady load

Notes:
- “Throughput” is evaluated during steady segments only (burst segments excluded unless explicitly stated).
- If tokens/s is not available, use requests/s only if output length distributions are identical and verified.

### Gate D: Stability / backlog growth
Applies to MW-3 and MW-4.

Fail if either:
1) Queue depth exhibits unbounded growth over the measurement window (positive slope sustained for > 3 minutes)
2) Timeout/drop rate increases by > **0.05% absolute** for S-class or L-class

## Required artifacts (what to attach to the perf report)
Each run must include:
- A summary table per scenario with p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and E2E by class
- Throughput (tokens/s) and utilization
- A “tail breakdown” view (queue wait vs service time) for S-class p95
- A note on kernel selection stability (confirm no unintended kernel drift, or document why drift occurred)
- Links to dashboards/traces if run in perf-canary infrastructure

## Where this runs (pipelines)
- **CI gate (required for scope changes):** `runtime-perf-ci` (mixed workload suite)
- **Pre-release validation:** `perf-canary` A/B job (baseline vs change) for at least MW-1 and MW-3

The benchmark harness must output a machine-readable summary (JSON) with:
- scenario name
- model + SKU
- class metrics
- baseline reference hash
- pass/fail per gate

## Exception process
If a change is expected to violate a gate (e.g., deliberate trade-off for correctness), an exception can be granted only with:
- Written approval from **Perf Program Owner (Jonas Weber)** and **Serving Runtime EM for Scheduling (Sofia Ivanova)**
- Documented mitigation plan (follow-up ticket + rollback plan)
- Explicit communication to SRE if the change could impact SLOs during canary

Exceptions must be time-bounded (max 2 release trains) and must include a plan to restore compliance.

## Ownership and updates
- Standard owner: Perf Program (Jonas Weber)
- Runtime implementation partner: Serving Runtime Scheduling (Sofia Ivanova)
- Benchmark harness owner: Rina Kobayashi
- SLO interpretation/rollback guidance: Sean Gallagher

This standard should be revisited quarterly or whenever we materially change:
- default scheduling policy
- supported max context length in production
- primary production GPU SKU

## Changelog
- 2025-02-03: Added MW-4 overload scenario and explicit recovery requirement; clarified throughput bounds for burst scenarios.
- 2025-01-14: Initial draft standard (MW-1..MW-3, Gates A–C).
